title: Hunts FH-002S: A capped check-in code admits two members at its last unit

source.ref: Split from FH-002 (2026-11-16): the last-unit scarcity race was reproduced; the legacy cap is not atomic.

detail:
A node with max_claims set (first N win, ADR-112) is enforced by a count in lib/engagement/verify.ts and a later insert in lib/engagement/capture.ts. Nothing holds the node between the two and each member has a different ledger key, so two members who scan together at the last unit both pass the count: two capture rows, two ledger rows, two Zap awards against a cap of one. A member arriving after them is refused, so the cap only fails inside the window. scripts/probes/hunts/legacy-seams.mjs reproduces it with the shipped orchestrators against the in-memory fixture (no database was raced). Owed, by Engagement with the owner's call on which: make the cap atomic (one database function that locks the node, counts and inserts, or a constraint the insert can fail on) or retire max_claims in favour of Hunt reward stock (hunt_reward_grant already serialises on the reward row). Still unproven anywhere in CI: two live Postgres sessions racing hunt_reward_grant; supabase/tests/hunt_rewards.test.sql covers the sequential last unit and records a by-hand two-session check. Done when: two members competing for the last unit leave one capture and one award, and the probe passes. Requires: FH-002. Owner role: Engagement.

Closed 2026-11-16. A node with max_claims now claims its unit through public.node_capture_claim (supabase/migrations/20270346084000_node_capture_claim.sql): the node row lock, the replay check, the count, the ledger row and the capture row are one transaction, called by lib/engagement/capture.ts for capped nodes only. Uncapped nodes keep the earlier path. The probe proves what the shipped caller does with the function's answers against the in-memory fixture; the lock itself is proven by supabase/tests/node_capture_claim.test.sql (sequential) and by a run on a local Postgres 16 with only the four tables involved: two sessions at the last unit left one capture and one refusal, forty sessions against a cap of five left five, and the old order oversold as a control. Still owed by the owner: apply the migration to production. Until then the caller gets function-not-found and falls back to count-then-insert, so the live cap still oversells inside the window; the probe run prints that state too. Not done: no race on the production schema, no real capped code scanned, the two-session run is not in CI, and the two-session race of hunt_reward_grant named above is still unrun. Same shape, not fixed here: the once_global capture rule is also a count then an insert.
